newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope's would-be assassin sends get-well message.
newsitem.headline: Pope's would-be assassin sends get-well message.

text.p: The Turkish gunman who almost killed Pope John Paul in 1981 sent him a telegram from jail on Monday saying he is praying for the Pontiff before his appendix operation, his defence lawyer said on Monday.

Mehmet Ali Agca, who is serving a life sentence at Ancona prison in eastern Italy, sent the message to the Gemelli hospital in Rome where the Polish-born Pope, 76, is due to have surgery on Tuesday, Agca's lawyer Marina Magistrelli said.
"Dearest Karol Wojtyla, I am spiritually close to you. I am praying for you," the telegram said.
"Only the eternal God Almighty can end our mysterious ordeal, since the horrendous Satan continues his persecution..," Magistrelli's office quoted the message as saying.
"I look forward to a second meeting. Please accept my deep esteem and fraternal best wishes," it concluded.
The Pope was rushed to the Gemelli for life-saving surgery after Agca shot him in the stomach during a general audience in St Peter's Square on May 13, 1981.
The Pope later visited Agca in prison to forgive him. It was not clear whether he had received the telegram at the Gemelli.
Agca's lawyer announced last month that her client had asked the Italian authorities for a pardon or a reduction in his sentence and the right to serve it out in a Turkish jail.
